newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: MBF Capital merger plan disapproved.
newsitem.headline: MBF Capital merger plan disapproved.

text.p: MBf Capital Bhd said that its application to Malaysia's central bank Bank Negara to start talks with Suria Capital Bhd for a "corporate exercise" has been disallowed.
The companies had submitted a proposal to Malaysian authorities to begin talks for a possible merger.
In a statement sent late on Monday to the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange, MBf Capital also sought to maintain the suspension of its stock "until further notice".
Rumours surfaced nearly two months ago that MBf Capital and Suria Capital could be looking at some form of merger, primarily concerning Suria's unit Sabah Bank Bhd.
Such a merger would result in MBf Capital holding a banking license.
But speculation surfaced this week that the deal would be called off because of Bank Negara's opposition to it.
In the statement, MBf said the application to Bank Negara to start talks for the corporate exercise with Suria "was not approved by Bank Negara Malaysia". It did not provide any reasons.
Suria Capital stock was down two cents to 2.68 ringgit at 0250 GMT, while MBf Capital's stock closed at 5.20 ringgit on June 6.
